headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; LangGraph’s default orchestration can amplify AutoGPT outputs into unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and LangGraph exposes application-defined files plus stdin/stdout and developer-wired nodes, so a shared workspace can let attacker-controlled content flow from A into B as trusted input. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented for either agent, so the pathway is plausible in default pairings.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or file tree
IF LangGraph nodes consume AutoGPT-generated files or stdout without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Add a provenance tag to every inter-agent artifact
Require manual review before B ingests A outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing adapters between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, while LangGraph reads application-defined files and can send data to model providers. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive material can flow from A into B and then out through B’s provider calls. The profiles do not show data-class restrictions or isolation, so leakage is plausible.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets, customer data, or regulated records
IF B forwards A-produced file contents into model-provider calls
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and mounts
Keep secrets out of shared directories
Restrict B to redacted inputs only
Review outbound prompts before provider calls
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on B egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, and both can write or mutate filesystem state in overlapping ways; LangGraph also supports multiple instances with shared checkpointer state. AutoGPT lacks multiple-instance support, but that does not prevent conflicts when paired with B on the same resources. Concurrent writes can corrupt files or shared state by default.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or checkpointer-backed state
IF either agent runs concurrently with the other on shared mutable resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths per agent
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared state
Snapshot state before each run
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is explicitly a graph of nodes where each node may itself be an agent, so it can readily treat AutoGPT outputs as inputs to downstream actions. AutoGPT can generate unverified content, and B can route that content into tools or model-provider calls without a documented verification barrier. That creates a default cascade from A’s output into B’s actions.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as node input or tool arguments
IF downstream nodes act on A outputs without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Insert a validation step between A and B
Require citations or schema checks on A outputs
Limit B to read-only evaluation of A outputs
Log and review all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add policy gates before any tool-executing node

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGPT is open-source and unverified, while LangGraph is a library that can route data to model providers and stores graph state in application-defined backends. The pair can therefore create retention and residency mismatches if regulated data enters B’s checkpointer or provider calls. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in LangGraph checkpointer state
IF provider calls from B transmit data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B state
Configure short retention on checkpointer storage
Use a compliant provider for B
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls
